start.card:
At a college, there are six times as many students as professors.
Let S be the number of students and P the number of professors. Which equation says the same thing? Pick one first.
start.title: Six times as many students

afterGuess.card:
You picked S = 6P. Now check it by putting in numbers.
Here is a small college: count 2 professors and 12 students. Then press each equation to plug the numbers in.
afterGuess.title: Six times as many students

after.card:
Now there are 6 professors and 36 students. Look at the table: which equation still works?
Takeaway: "six times as many students as professors" is S = 6P. The 6 goes with the smaller group (professors) to make it as big as the bigger group (students). When unsure, put in numbers.
after.title: Six times as many students
